Remember to pay attention to your attention. Allow it to be open and free, so that your awareness will expand, your suffering will shrink, and your joy will grow. Open it by letting go of anything that could restrict it from going where it needs to go. Free it by unshackling it from control and by allowing it to move when it needs to move.
Notice your attachments to your intentions — to your strongest desires, aversions, and beliefs. Notice how your attention returns to these same intentions over and over again. Notice also the kinds of suffering that you experience — persistent feelings of regret, stress, anxiety, frustration, anger, despair, grief, and many more.
Recognize the connection between your suffering and your attachments, and how the former arises when your attention is controlled by the latter. Set your attention free from all of the thoughts, feelings, memories, and imaginings that arise in you again and again. Notice how often your attention settles on thoughts about your intentions and how difficult it can be to set it free again.

Collectible furniture meets cultural critique at Dutch Design Week’s Table of Power
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-25
06:00:00 UTC
15:00:00 KST

Collectible furniture meets cultural critique at Dutch Design Week’s Table of Power
Show Not Show has put a twist on a classic project documenting the echelons of power with an exhibition of the design collective’s furniture at Dutch Design Week.
Held at the Kruisruimte exhibition space in Eindhoven, The Table of Power exhibition takes inspiration from Jacqueline Hassink’s 1990s photo series of the same name.
This saw the photographer document the boardrooms of Fortune 500 companies, empty of people.
As in those photographs, The Table of Power has a long table at its centre as a symbol of institutional authority.
In this case, the table seems to stretch eternally into the horizon, thanks to the mirror placed at the far end.
Designed especially for the exhibition by collective members Frank Penders and Luuk van Laarhoven, the table is made from sheet metal, cut and bent into a brutalist form, with brushed textures and chromatic gradients adding allure.
Around it, collectible furniture, lighting and textile pieces from fellow members Lucas Zito, Marc Meeuwissen, Mokko and Studio Fabius Clovis as well as guest exhibitors Aleksandra Adamchyk, Kilian Vos and Pablo Octavio fill the room with a mix of raw wood, glossy lacquer, sculptural metal and translucent glowing bioplastic.
The idea for the exhibition came after Show Not Show were invited to host Dutch Design Week’s official press dinner.
“Our exhibition space isn’t that big,” said Penders. “So we decided to do something quite simple: instead of fitting a dinner into our exhibition, we made the dinner the starting point for the exhibition.”
In Show Not Show’s vision, the press represents a site of power in the design industry, influencing what gets seen, discussed and remembered, and their presence completes the exhibition’s concept.
Guests at the dinner were encouraged to get up from the table from time to time to “share the power”, but Dezeen observed that few journalists ever got up.
Penders told Dezeen that The Table of Power continues Show Not Show’s practice of using exhibitions to explore aspects of the design world that are not commonly seen.
“Each exhibition offers a glimpse into our world as designers, revealing something that visitors might not normally see or consider,” Penders told Dezeen. “In 2024, we showed our experiments and prototypes. In 2025, we focused on the ideas and concepts behind our work.”
“This year, the subject is visibility. Being seen, becoming known and finding recognition for what you create. It is about the relationship between designers, their work and the media that bring it to a wider audience.”
In addition to the table, Octavio’s curtain-like brushed aluminium room dividers are given a symbolic role to play in the exhibition. Their height allows those sitting down greater oversight of the room than their standing peers, adding to the sense of power imbalance.
Key pieces in the exhibition include a new series of angular wooden stools called Barricada, designed by Meewissen to match the dining table seating. Like all of his works, they are made with just one tool and one material.
There is also characterful plywood furniture by Studio Fabius Clovis, its uneven surface highlighted with high-gloss lacquer, and totemic pendant lights by Lucas Zito, 3D printed from bioplastic and playing with the spatial effects of unexpected scale.
Guest exhibitors Adamchyk, Vos and Octavio continue the elemental mood, bringing their sculptural zigzagging Waveform drawer, geological Future Fossils rugs and stone-like but squishy Lapis lounge chair respectively.
Show Not Show launched in 2024 and has exhibited at the Kruisruimte each year since. It has also taken its shows abroad with presentations at the Design Biennale Rotterdam, Collectible Brussels and Milan design week.
Elsewhere at Dutch Design Week, Boris Acket and Maison the Faux have staged the moody and maximalist installation Everything Moist Seems Alive at the MU Hybrid Art House, complete with performances from the Dutch National Opera and Ballet.
Dutch Design Week 2026 takes place from 17 to 25 October 2026 at various locations across Eindhoven, the Netherlands. See Dezeen Events Guide for more architecture and design events around the world.
Photography by Show Not Show

DPP urges vigilance against Chinese election meddling
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-25
05:57:41 UTC
14:57:41 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The DPP China Affairs Department warned that the rise of Puma Shen’s (沈伯洋) mayoral campaign has drawn significant attention from China, which it warned is covertly and overtly interfering with Taiwan’s elections.
The DPP said the public must be particularly vigilant against two types of election interference, including disinformation and political intimidation, according to a party Facebook post.
Disinformation may range from fake opinion polls with unknown sources and audio or video clips taken out of context to fabricated scandals, romantic rumors, and false deepfake reports of candidates withdrawing from races, the DPP said. Such content may be disseminated en masse shortly before voting, when there is little time to verify its accuracy. The more sensational a claim is, and the more urgently it urges people to “share immediately,” the more important it is to pause and check the facts first, the party said.
Political intimidation includes threats, surveillance, and attacks targeting candidates, their relatives, and their supporters, the DPP said. These attacks can restrict people’s ability to participate freely in politics, it added.
The party said Taiwan's law enforcement should investigate the masterminds and funding sources behind such cases. The public must be aware of attempts to incite retaliation using unverified information, which could further escalate tensions, it said.
The DPP stressed that Beijing accuses Taiwan of democratic disorder while simultaneously manipulating information and applying political pressure. Its aim is to undermine mutual trust within society and weaken public confidence in the democratic system, the party said.
Elections must be decided by the Taiwanese alone, the DPP said, adding that Beijing must not be allowed to influence their choices through disinformation and intimidation.

Typhoon Champi causes NT$133 million in agricultural losses
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-25
05:09:15 UTC
14:09:15 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Typhoon Champi caused an estimated NT$133.36 million (US$4.2 million) in agricultural losses across Taiwan, with Yunlin County accounting for 82% of the total, according to the Ministry of Agriculture.
Yunlin County recorded the largest losses at NT$109.6 million, followed by Yilan County at NT$8.39 million, New Taipei at NT$7.24 million, Taoyuan at NT$3.46 million, Taichung at NT$2.64 million and Hualien County at NT$1.96 million, per CNA.
Among agricultural products, garlic suffered the greatest losses, estimated at NT$53.07 million. The crop sustained damage across 326 hectares, with a reported damage severity of 39%, equivalent to about 126 hectares of total crop loss.
Overall, 2,405 hectares of farmland were affected, with an average damage severity of 25%, equivalent to 594 hectares of total crop loss. Other affected crops included peanuts, onions, sweet corn, and tea.
Strong winds and heavy rain caused crop leaves to turn yellow or tear, plants to fall over, and vegetation to wilt, according to an Agriculture and Food Agency report.
Damage to private agricultural facilities was estimated at NT$290,000, mainly due to torn plastic coverings on greenhouses. About 5 hectares were affected, with an estimated damage rate of 30%.
Agricultural officials have pledged to speed up damage assessments and relief efforts to help affected farmers get back on their feet and resume production. The ministry said assessments were ongoing, so the final damage estimates could change as more reports are processed.

RBI's data centre at Jatni would be the second of its kind, after the one in Navi Mumbai (Photo: ANI).
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Reserve Bank of India's Rs 169-crore data centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar on Sunday, officials said.Chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi said in a social media post on Saturday that the facility would add to Odisha's development journey. "The visit of the Honourable Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modiji to Odisha and the inauguration of RBI's state-of-the-art data centre will not only strengthen the state's digital infrastructure but also give new momentum to the security of the country's financial data and the growth of the digital economy," he said in the post on Saturday.Majhi added that the RBI's data centre at Jatni would be the second of its kind, after the one in Navi Mumbai. The PM last visited the state four months ago, when he attended an event marking two years of the BJP government in Odisha. PTI reported.
Officials said the facilities have been designed to meet the central bank's computing requirements and to offer a secure, resilient, scalable and future-ready computing ecosystem for the bank and the wider financial sector.According to a government statement, the data centre will house mission-critical payment and settlement systems, besides other flagship initiatives.
It will help widen the reach, efficiency and reliability of digital financial services, and will serve as the secure digital foundation on which India's increasingly technology-driven financial economy can grow, the statement said.Similarly, the Cybersecurity Training Institute will strengthen capability building by providing a dedicated institutional platform for cybersecurity and enterprise-technology training, research and sector-wide capability development, it added.The RBI facility is spread over 18.55 acres. Its foundation stone was laid on March 22, 2023, by the then RBI governor Shaktikanta Das. An official said the site at Info Valley-II was selected for its geographical stability, as it lies away from seismically active zones and high-risk international border areas, thereby reducing exposure to natural disasters and geopolitical vulnerabilities. PTI reported
As per the schedule, Modi will land at Biju Patnaik International Airport at around 4.10 pm aboard a special Indian Air Force aircraft, officials said. He will then travel by helicopter to Khurda, and from there proceed by road to the RBI facility at Info Valley-II in Jatni.The Prime Minister is expected to spend about an hour at the data centre before returning to the airport by road. He is due to depart at around 6.30 pm.According to PTI, Police have made elaborate security arrangements for the visit, with around 2,100 personnel deployed. Traffic restrictions will also be in force from 5.40 pm to 6.40 pm on the route linking the RBI data centre with the airport.

Unknown Publisher

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday announced a major crackdown on an international narcotics cartel, with Operation Trident targeting 38 locations across Assam, Mizoram and Manipur.The operation, that took place on October 23, uncovered hawala transactions worth Rs 100 crore and resulted in the freezing of 1,424 bank accounts and the attachment of properties valued at Rs 17.82 crore. Officials also seized 500 detonators and Rs 12 lakh in cash, while 18 people were arrested.Announcing the operation on X, Shah said that the cartel was trafficking narcotics across India, Myanmar and Bangladesh through the Death Triangle Corridor. He credited the central agencies and police forces of the three states for the crackdown.“Modi Govt deals another lethal blow against drugs with Operation Trident,” Shah said in his post.
He said that the agencies had launched coordinated crackdowns across the three states, dismantling the international network and uncovering its financial transactions. The operation, he added, was part of the Centre's mission to eliminate every drug network in the country by December 31, 2029.
“The offensive attests to India’s Himalayan resolve to realise the mission of eradicating every drug network by 31 December 2029. India will hammer until the last nail is driven into the coffin of drug cartels,” Shah said.Congratulating the anti-narcotics team, the home minister acknowledged the role of central agencies and the police forces of Assam, Mizoram and Manipur in the operation.“Heartiest congratulations to the anti-narcotics team comprising central agencies, and police forces of the three states.”
Centre targets drug networks by December 2029
The operation comes amid the Centre's push to eliminate drug networks from the country by December 31, 2029. Shah has said that the home ministry will dedicate the remaining part of 2026 and the following three years to freeing the country from the drug menace.He has also called on police forces across the country to participate wholeheartedly in implementing the Nasha Mukt Bharat roadmap.At the third National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) heads of states and Union territories in New Delhi in September, Shah said the country would collectively succeed in uprooting the drug trade by December 31, 2029.He emphasised coordinated action, clear targets and accountability, along with the need to dismantle drug networks. Protecting young people from substance abuse, he said, was also important to achieving the national vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047.
Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan reaches over 35 crore people
The Centre's anti-drug efforts also include the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, implemented by the ministry of social justice and empowerment under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR).As on date, the campaign has reached more than 35 crore people, including over 13.94 crore young people and 10.86 crore women. It has also engaged with more than 32 lakh educational institutions.Launched on August 15, 2020, the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan initially covered 272 vulnerable districts before expanding its reach across the country. The campaign places particular emphasis on young people, women and communities, recognising their role in preventing substance use and promoting healthy lifestyles.

After falling behind 3-0 in the four-game series, the Diamonds will be playing for pride at Melbourne's John Cain Arena on Wednesday.
The Diamonds are also a chance of losing their world number one netball ranking to New Zealand after the Ferns won gold at the Commonwealth Games in August, while Australia claimed bronze.
Head coach Stacey Marinkovich now has just a 50 per cent series winning record in the Constellation Cup.
Before she took charge in 2020, the Silver Ferns had claimed the trophy once in 10 series. In the six series since, the Kiwis have claimed it three times.
Marinkovich is contracted through to the end of 2027. This is the last time her team will be together before next August for the Netball World Cup in Sydney.
The result looks ominous for the Diamonds' chances.
However, former Diamond Bianca Chatfield believes Marinkovich's role is safe, alluding to the challenges of the unlimited import rule in Australia's Super Netball league.
"I think she's safe for now … unlike male sports there's not the money just to pay out coaches and get rid of them, and you do that in the heat of the moment," Chatfield told ABC's Offsiders.
"She deserves a chance to go through to the World Cup … She's facing different pressures to what other Australian coaches have in the past."
New Zealand head coach Noeline Taurua said the victory was a massive result for the Ferns after a challenging 12 months.
Taurua was suspended from coaching her team this time last year by Netball New Zealand and missed tours of Australia, England and Scotland before being reinstated.
The New Zealand Premiership has also been in fast decline due to poor broadcast deals and management by the national body. Most Silver Ferns jumped ship and signed with Australian teams to ensure they could earn a full-time wage.
"This is our opportunity to write the next chapter of our book," Taurua said.
"Commonwealth Games gold was obviously the start of that and now backing that up with the Constellation Cup.
"Whether the world number one [is next] or not, we're within cooee of Australia and getting closer, knowing that we're building towards the World Cup.
"We're just riding the wave and enjoying the moment."

The start is important
Speaking on Friday in Sydney, Marinkovich told ABC Sport reporter Amanda Shalala that the biggest lesson the team has taken from the opening matches is to get the start of the match right.
"For us, we've really got to be able to take the first five minutes of the quarters," she said.
"I think they've got little jumps on us in those moments. We've got to really solidify ball that we do get and make sure that we do put it on the scoreboard to pass some of that pressure back to New Zealand."
Lopsided penalty count
Australia has been heavily penalised throughout the series and Stacey Marinkovich said her team would be looking for clarification from the umpires as to why that is.
New Zealand has conceded 100 penalties so far, while the Diamonds have conceded 145. That's a lot of time standing beside your player, unable to contribute to play.
The same two umpires will officiate all four games of the series: Gary Burgess (English) and Alison Harrison (Welsh).
But Marinkovich told the media that she felt the Diamonds were umpired differently on home soil. Whether the coach agrees or not, they definitely need to be more disciplined today.
"In history, for the last four years, we've been penalised in New Zealand and it kind of shifts when we're in Australia … But I don't think our game plan changes too differently."

Taiwan tallies damage after Typhoon Champi
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-25
04:18:28 UTC
13:18:28 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Typhoon Champi left one person dead and 616 injured as it moved away from Taiwan on Saturday, with authorities reporting thousands of incidents of damage, widespread power outages, and nearly 5,000 evacuations.
The Central Emergency Operation Center said the single fatality involved a man who was swept away by waves on a beach in Liuqiu Township, Pingtung County. Most injuries were minor, including abrasions and contusions, according to the center, per CNA.
As of 4:30 p.m. Saturday, authorities had received 9,027 reports of damage, with 3,146 cases still being processed. The most common incidents involve fallen trees, damaged infrastructure, downed power lines, and fallen advertising signs, the CEOC said.
Although the storm's center did not make landfall, it came within 1 km of Taiwan's northeastern coast, bringing strong winds and heavy rain, per LTN.
More than 340,000 households lost electricity during the storm, with about 22,000 still awaiting repairs Saturday evening. Another 1,581 landline services and 204 mobile base stations required repairs, per a CEOC press release.
Rainfall was particularly heavy in the country's north and northeast. Yilan County recorded 650 millimeters of accumulated rainfall from Thursday through 4 p.m. Saturday, while Taoyuan and Hsinchu counties each received more than 500 mm. Taipei recorded 469.5 mm, according to the CEOC.
Authorities maintained yellow alerts for 46 streams in Taoyuan and Hsinchu and two areas in Hsinchu at risk of large-scale landslides.
The CEOC said it had evacuated 4,960 people from areas across Taiwan, including New Taipei, Taoyuan, Keelung, and Tainan cities, as well as Yilan, Hualien, Nantou, Yunlin, Pingtung, Hsinchu, Chiayi, and Taitung counties. Another 140 people were evacuated from the landslide-dammed lake on the Wanli River in Hualien County.
The storm also disrupted air travel, with hundreds of flights canceled at Taiwan Taoyuan International Airport on Friday and Saturday. The Ministry of Agriculture estimated agricultural losses at NT$133.36 million (US$4.2 million) as of Saturday afternoon, with Yunlin County accounting for more than 80% of the reported losses and garlic crops among the hardest hit, per CNA.
The central government downgraded the disaster response to Level 2 as the storm's immediate threat eased. The Ministry of Environment continues to assist local governments with post-disaster sanitation and recovery efforts.

Taiwan Army rolls out unscripted training to boost combat readiness
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-25
04:18:24 UTC
13:18:24 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The Army is implementing its new Combat Training Center 2.0 program to replace the traditional model of short, concentrated evaluations and scripted exercises.
The new program centers on three main principles: abandoning scorecards, transforming evaluators' roles, and conducting unscripted training, per CNA.
Commanders establish their own training objectives and evaluation criteria based on their units’ actual capabilities and operational missions. The battalion, brigade, and training center must first review the criteria. They must meet the minimum requirements stipulated in military regulations.
Instructors also move from the traditional role of “evaluators” to that of “observers.” All undergo observer, coach, and trainer training and observe battalion, company, and platoon-level operations throughout the exercise, without compromising safety, according to CNA.
They will order units to repeat tasks they perform poorly to help soldiers absorb combat lessons through hands-on experience.
The program emphasizes coordinated operations across different units, CNA reported. Instructors said CTC 2.0 seeks to address historically weak coordination between units by requiring friendly forces to plan missions together, establish communications links, and clarify support requirements.
After completing base training, units move on to joint exercises, including joint live-fire assessments, brigade-level force-on-force drills, and defense plan rehearsals.

Will China’s 4 peace principles for tackling African conflicts work?

Will China’s 4 peace principles for tackling African conflicts work?
Beijing seeks to safeguard billions in regional infrastructure and economic investments while hewing to its pledge of non-interference
Chinese President Xi Jinping outlined Beijing’s formula for tackling African conflicts and hot-button issues during a meeting this month with visiting Togolese leader Faure Gnassingbe, framing it around four principles linking peace to development.
The principles focus on African-led security free from outside intervention; upholding sovereignty and UN Charter principles; rejecting force and sanctions and favouring ceasefires through dialogue; and focusing on both immediate security concerns and long-term development.
Asked last week whether the principles could be applied to northern Ethiopia and the heightened tensions with neighbouring Eritrea, Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said they offered “practical guidance” for the Horn of Africa.

Will AI-powered open-door vending machines reshape Hong Kong’s retail landscape?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-25
04:00:15 UTC
13:00:15 KST

Will AI-powered open-door vending machines reshape Hong Kong’s retail landscape?
Smart coolers offer seamless grab-and-go convenience, but local operators say city’s distinct economic factors may stall widespread adoption
Sherry Shum has embraced a new shopping routine after finding a smart vending machine near her home in Chai Wan in Hong Kong.
The 37-year-old retail worker uses her phone to scan a QR code, opens the smart machine’s door, picks up a bottle of Coca-Cola, an oolong tea and a pack of potato chips, closes it and walks away with HK$60 (US$7.70) worth of goods. The whole process is so seamless that the bulk of the time is spent deciding what to buy.
The moment Shum takes an item from the shelf, the machine detects the product based on its appearance and debits her account. Once she shuts the door, the bill is settled via the payment method she selected before opening it.
“I buy things basically every day … I can grab multiple items at once after just opening the door,” she said. “The open-door machines are more convenient because you do not have to wait for items to drop one by one from traditional machines that sometimes get stuck.”

Gulf economies accelerate diversification as recession looms over Iran war

Tom Hussainin Islamabad
Before the outbreak of the war triggered by the US-Israeli attack on Iran in February, the Gulf monarchies were living the prosperity dream that was the envy of the world.
Their hydrocarbon-fuelled economies were glitzy oases of growth, inoculated from the conflict in Gaza that had rocked other parts of the Middle East for several years.
Underpinned by decades-old US security guarantees and conflict mediation by billionaire sheikhs, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar cultivated images as peaceful lands of opportunity as they invested staggering amounts of money in economic diversification programmes.
Backed by sovereign wealth funds with trillions of dollars invested mostly in the West, these leading states of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) embarked on transformative programmes to reposition their economies amid the global transition away from oil and gas. Similar diversification initiatives were also happening in Kuwait, Oman and Bahrain, the other three GCC members.

The Public Health Consequences of an Inaccurate Census
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-25
04:00:03 UTC
13:00:03 KST

In 2015, Chicago’s public health department identified three cases of invasive meningococcal disease, a highly dangerous pathogen that can kill within hours. To determine whether these cases signaled a larger outbreak, the department—which one of us, Dr. Julie Morita, led at the time—needed to know not just total cases, but the total population and demographics of affected areas. The team turned to a pillar of our nation’s public health system: the U.S. Census.
The data showed that men who have sex with men—including gay and bisexual men—among the city’s Black population were disproportionately affected. That finding drove the health department’s response, which included working with community partners to surge thousands of free vaccines into neighborhoods across Chicago. Instead of a larger and far deadlier outbreak, the outbreak ended with 11 cases in Chicago and one death.
Census data informs every aspect of our nation’s public health system. As former leaders of local and federal health agencies, we have seen this firsthand. Unfortunately, the Trump Administration has proposed radical changes to the census that would make our country less healthy, less safe, and less fair.
The public comment period on this proposal closes on Nov. 2. Health leaders must move quickly to oppose these deeply misguided changes. It is clear to us that these changes would amount not only to an assault on our public health system but also on the U.S. Constitution.
Per the Constitution, the federal government has carried out a national census every decade since 1790—through wars, depressions, and pandemics. Everyone who resides in our country matters and should be counted. But the Trump Administration is suggesting that the census should intentionally exclude people. This includes undocumented residents and nonimmigrant visa holders, such as foreign national students and temporary workers whose visas may permit them to live in the U.S. for several years. The Administration is further attempting to remove demographic questions related to race, ethnicity, and sexual orientation from the census questionnaire.
The repercussions would be vast. An inaccurate count would negatively affect congressional representation. The idea that some people do not deserve to be counted uncomfortably echoes the “3/5 compromise,” an insidious and later repealed clause in the original Constitution under which enslaved persons were counted as less than full people. Incomplete and unreliable demographic data could distort how trillions of federal dollars are distributed across hundreds of programs such as Medicaid, SNAP, WIC, and Head Start. Communities with the greatest needs, especially those with immigrant or mixed-status families, would likely be hardest hit.
These are our neighbors, families, and friends. But let’s be clear: the impacts would extend beyond those communities, especially the public health consequences. As the Chicago meningococcal outbreak illustrates, health officials need a complete picture to protect people from disease and other threats. They must know who is getting sick, where, and at what rate. Take any of those data out of the equation, and the people who need the most help are far less likely to get it.
During the H1N1 influenza pandemic in 2009, when one of us, Dr. Richard Besser, served as acting director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), census data were instrumental in tracking the outbreak. CDC relied on this data to calculate infection rates by age, which showed that children and young adults were getting sick at far higher rates than older adults—a striking departure from typical patterns observed with seasonal flu. When a vaccine became available, these data directly informed recommendations that prioritized children and young adults.
A decade later, the COVID pandemic demonstrated the importance of these data on a massive scale. As case counts surged in the initial months of the outbreak, population and demographic data revealed who was shouldering the greatest burdens. CDC found that hospitalization rates were highest for American Indian, Alaska Native, Black, and Hispanic populations. CDC later used census population estimates to calculate vaccination rates by race and ethnicity, allowing health officials to identify disparities in vaccine uptake. States like North Carolina relied successfully on census-tract data to increase vaccination rates among target populations.
These examples span different locations, diseases, and levels of government, but illustrate common themes: public health officials rely heavily on census data to save lives and protect communities, and protecting communities at greatest risk helps keep us all safer and healthier.
Health officials use population counts to study cancer, heart disease, HIV/AIDS, and many other diseases. Demographic data expose disparities that raw numbers can obscure and show whether those gaps are growing or shrinking. Together, they offer a roadmap to direct resources where they can do the most good.
The next census count is still a few years away, but what our leaders decide now matters a great deal. A census that deliberately counts fewer people while telling us less about them will leave our nation ill-prepared for future outbreaks and pandemics, while making it harder to handle daily health challenges. It is essential for the public health community to speak out now.

NAGOYA, Japan, Oct. 25 (Xinhua) -- After a week of fierce competition, Chinese athletes concluded the 2026 Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, on Saturday with strong results and several notable moments.
China sent 312 athletes, averaging 28.8 years old, as part of a 500-member delegation to its fifth Asian Para Games, competing in 335 events across 17 sports.
With 207 gold medals, 117 silver and 111 bronze for a total of 435 medals, China posted its best result at an overseas Asian Para Games and topped the gold and overall medal standings for a fifth consecutive time. Chinese athletes also set 11 world records and 18 Asian records.
On Monday, the first competition day after the opening ceremony, 39-year-old Cui Zhe claimed China's first gold medal of the Games in the women's 41kg para powerlifting. She has competed at all five editions of the Asian Para Games and won gold at each.
After that, China's national anthem echoed frequently at venues across Nagoya. At several medal ceremonies, three Chinese flags were raised side by side as Chinese athletes swept the podium.
"We always give it our all in the pool. We really want to see three Chinese national flags raised together," said Zheng Tingting after winning the women's 400m freestyle S8, with training partners Zhu Hui and Lu Weiyuan taking silver and bronze in the same race. "In training, we push each other and share what we've learned from competing."
Swimmers led China's haul with 64 golds from 79 events. Track and field athletes contributed another 54, with four Chinese athletes setting world records.
China also excelled in para badminton, table tennis, fencing and cycling, while the wheelchair tennis team won gold in both women's singles and doubles, marking its best-ever result at the Asian Para Games.
Yet as Asian Paralympic Committee President Majid Rashed noted at Saturday night's closing ceremony, "These numbers reflect remarkable achievements. But the true success of these Games is found in the athletes who made them possible."
Their courage to compete and determination to give their best are inspiring in their own right, he said.
Para cyclist Liu Qiangli braved a sudden downpour to familiarize himself with the course before clocking the fastest time in the men's H1-5 individual time trial.
Sprinter Deng Peicheng competed through injury to break a long-standing world record in the men's 100m T36 final.
Like Cui, 40-year-old discus and shot put athlete Mi Na also won gold at her fifth consecutive Asian Para Games.
For many athletes, sport has brought far more than medals. It has changed their lives. Speaking after their events, several described how it had rekindled their passion for life, restored their confidence and given them a sense of purpose.
Para taekwondo gold medalist Li Yujie, one of China's flagbearers at the Games' opening ceremony, reflected on taking up the sport and pushing through tough training.
"It's these moments that have made me stronger, more confident and better able to take life's challenges in stride," she said. "That's something I truly treasure."
Dong Shunjiang, 34, lost part of his right leg in the devastating 2008 Wenchuan earthquake, buried under rubble while trying to save younger schoolmates. He never gave up on life despite the hardships. In Nagoya, at his third Asian Para Games, he won bronze in the men's wheelchair tennis singles, his best result at the Games.
"Through playing tennis, I have gradually regained my confidence in life and returned to the positive mindset I used to have," Dong said. "I no longer feel inferior because of my disability. I hope to take part in more competitions, improve my skills, and achieve better results."
The Asian Para Games has come to a close, but China's para athletes are continuing their journey. Many are already setting their sights on the next goal: the 2028 Paralympic Games in Los Angeles. ■

Japan's planned security publicity campaign raises concerns

TOKYO, Oct. 25 (Xinhua) -- Japan's government plans to step up public outreach on security policy from late October, targeting different age groups with tailored messaging as it prepares to revise its three key security documents by the end of this year, Kyodo News reported Saturday, a move that has raised concerns in Japan.
The government plans to release videos produced in collaboration with public figures on the internet and social media to reach younger audiences. Advertisements will also be placed on Tokyo subway trains and at Shibuya Crossing, a major intersection in the capital, highlighting the links between national security and everyday life.
For middle-aged and older audiences, the campaign will use social media, television and shopping mall advertisements to explain how security policy relates to family and personal safety, the report said.
The Japanese government plans to revise its three key national security documents by the end of 2026, with "new ways of warfare" and sustained combat capabilities expected to be among the key focuses. The revision is also expected to set a target for further increases in defense spending.
Kyodo News reported that the campaign could provoke a backlash if it is perceived as an attempt to steer public opinion in favor of specific policies, potentially evoking memories of prewar Japan.
Ukeru Magosaki, a former Japanese Foreign Ministry official, said Japan was witnessing developments reminiscent of the prewar period, including militarization, control over public discourse, the neglect of vulnerable groups and the incitement of hostility toward neighboring countries.
Magosaki said the government's intensified publicity drive was intended to strengthen Japan's military capabilities and position the country as a "pawn" of the United States. ■

First-placed Pieter Devos (C) of Belgium, second-placed Olivier Philippaerts (L) of Belgium and third-placed Ben Maher of Britain pose for a group photo during the awarding ceremony for the CSI5 1.60m competition of the Global Champions Tour Grand Prix of Cairo at the Great Pyramids, Giza, Egypt on Oct. 24, 2026. CAIRO, Oct. 25 (Xinhua) -- Belgian rider Pieter Devos won the Global Champions Tour Grand Prix of Cairo on Saturday, bringing the international show-jumping circuit's first Egyptian leg to a close against the backdrop of the Great Pyramids of Giza.
Riding his homebred mare Casual DV Z, Devos completed a clear jump-off round in 45.85 seconds to win the 1.60-meter Grand Prix and claim the 1 million euro prize. His compatriot Olivier Philippaerts finished second on Hipster SV, while Britain's Ben Maher took third aboard Point Break.
Large crowds gathered over the three-day event to watch the competition, as horses and riders lined up for their turns in the arena with the pyramids rising behind the course.
For Devos, the victory carried personal significance. Casual DV Z had previously secured several podium finishes in five-star Grand Prix competitions but had yet to claim a win.
"She's just something very exceptional," Devos told Xinhua. "We made the first-ever show in Cairo...it is the first Grand Prix win for my horse, so with Casual, we are very happy today."
Devos said he had been surprised by the number of fans who came to watch and praised the organizers for providing good conditions for horses and riders. He described the event as a promising start for future editions and said he would return.
Hosting the tour for the first time also gave Egypt an opportunity to showcase its historic landmarks and equestrian sport to an international audience, said Hany Magdy, spokesperson for the Egyptian Equestrian Federation.
Magdy said Egypt had secured an agreement to host the five-star championship annually for the next five years, with competitions planned in different locations across the country.
Aya Mohamed, a 26-year-old from Cairo who works in real estate sales, followed the competition for all three days. She has long loved horses and dreamed of becoming a rider, but never managed to turn that dream into reality.
She welcomed the championship's arrival in Egypt and said she looked forward to seeing it return in the coming years.
"I'm very proud that Egypt is hosting such a prestigious championship, and I'm happy that we'll have the chance to watch it here in the coming years," she told Xinhua. ■

SANTIAGO, Chile, Oct. 24 (Xinhua) -- China's Zhao Yicheng and Deng Lijuan won the men's and women's speed climbing titles at the World Climbing Series season finale in Santiago on Saturday, with world record holder Zhao also securing the men's overall season crown.
The 17-year-old Zhao finished only 12th in qualification but improved steadily through the knockout rounds, clocking 5.00, 4.81 and 4.79 seconds from the round of 16 to the semifinals.
He then won the gold medal race in 4.74 seconds, beating Indonesia's Raharjati Nursamsa.
Zhao said after the race that his disappointing qualifying performance had made him nervous, but advancing to the last 16 helped him regain his form and start enjoying the competition. He said he was satisfied with his final performance.
China's Chu Shouhong, fresh from winning gold at the Nagoya Asian Games, narrowly missed the podium in the bronze medal race. He clocked 4.96 seconds, losing to Japan's Ryo Omasa by 0.02 seconds.
Zhao made his World Climbing Series debut this season, winning two golds, one silver and one bronze across six events. He also set the men's speed climbing world record of 4.54 seconds at the season opener.
Omasa finished second in the men's overall standings, with Nursamsa third.
In the women's competition, Deng beat world record holder Emma Hunt of the United States in the gold medal race with a time of 6.38 seconds.
Deng, the silver medalist at the Paris 2024 Olympics, said she was delighted to win gold at the final event of the year. She said she had struggled early in the season and only began to show her true level in the final two events.
In the bronze medal race, Isis Rothfork of the United States clocked 7.32 seconds to beat China's Mou Yuju for third place.
Hunt finished atop the women's overall standings, ahead of Ukraine's Polina Khalkevych and Indonesia's Desak Made Rita Kusuma Dewi, the women's speed champion at the Nagoya Asian Games.
The Santiago event, held in Chile for the first time, attracted nearly 400 climbers from 95 countries and regions. It is the final stop of the 2026 World Climbing Series for speed and lead climbing.
The lead competition concludes on Sunday with the semifinals and finals. Slovenia's Janja Garnbret, a two-time Olympic champion, will seek her third individual title of the season. ■

LISBON – Portuguese police cleared a housing protest camp from the centre of Lisbon in the early hours of Oct 25, charging demonstrators and making several arrests, with minor injuries reported, though figures were not immediately available.
Portugal is grappling with one of Europe's most acute home affordability crises, as prices have more than doubled since 2017, while rents for new leases have nearly doubled, with young people among the hardest hit.
"We have an obligation to fight for what we believe in," said Vitor Gomes, 21, a multimedia communications student, adding that housing speculation, wealth concentration and rising inequality made him pessimistic about the future.
Shortly after 2am, dozens of officers moved in on the camp in Rossio Square, after warning protesters to remove their tents or face their dismantling, and threatening disobedience charges for those who resisted.
Protesters had pitched more than 100 tents after a protest march by thousands along one of the capital's main avenues.
Hundreds gathered to protect the encampment after police dismantled a similar camp there on Oct 20.
The police action was "completely disproportionate", as there had been no public disorder, said Left Bloc lawmaker Fabian Figueiredo.
"The worst thing that could happen was having this police force charge hundreds of people who are here peacefully. Why?" asked Figueiredo, who was at the camp.
Protesters say soaring rents and higher living costs are squeezing households and turning housing into a growing source of discontent.
The Bank of Portugal estimates a shortfall of 300,000 homes nationwide, equivalent to Lisbon's entire housing stock.
The protesters are demanding that the government scrap a bill to make evictions easier and end rent caps on new leases, which passed a first parliamentary reading, although the far-right Chega party abstained.
The protest followed similar demonstrations in Belgium, France, Italy and Spain. REUTERS

Sri Lanka Records Zero Prosecutions Amid Online Scam Surge
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-25
03:30:00 UTC
12:30:00 KST

Authorities in Sri Lanka have failed to successfully prosecute a single transnational cyber scam case, police have said, despite more than a thousand arrests so far this year of suspected members of Asian fraud syndicates who have surged into the South Asian country.
The admission comes as experts warn the island nation is becoming a destination of choice for thousands of scam workers fleeing Southeast Asian nations such as Cambodia, which had in recent years become home to massive scam compounds, many of them reliant on trafficked workers. 
Recently crackdowns in scam centers in Southeast Asia have driven mostly Chinese-origin scam syndicates to set up shop in vulnerable states from Madagascar to Papua New Guinea. 
Among the countries of South Asia, Sri Lanka stands out for being at “serious risk of becoming a hub for industrial-scale cyber scams,” the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime (GI-TOC) said last month.
From January until September, Sri Lankan police have conducted raids on 27 suspected scam compounds around the country and arrested 1093 people, Sri Lankan police spokesman Fredrick Wootler told OCCRP and Sri Lanka’s The Sunday Times.
The figure represents a dramatic rise from 2025, when just 26 people were arrested, Wootler said. An additional 573 suspected scammers were arrested the year prior.
Despite the well-publicized arrests, “we have not had a successful prosecution yet” of anyone suspected of using Sri Lanka as a base for scamming victims abroad, Wootler said.
The issue, Wootler explained, is that Sri Lanka’s current computer crime law, which dates from 2007, only allows cases to be opened on the basis of a complaint from a victim. Since the majority of those getting scammed live abroad, few complaints have been received.
Instead, he added, the vast majority of suspected scammers are being charged for visa violations and being removed from the country.
“The current government is …very much keen to see that this type of criminal networks [must] be taken away from Sri Lanka,” Wootler said.
The head of Sri Lanka’s police cyber crime unit, Chandima Arumapperuma, told reporters that the majority of suspects arrested so far carry passports from Asian countries such as China, Vietnam, India, and Indonesia. Many come with travel records showing they had previously been in Cambodia or Myanmar, both well-known scam hubs, she added.
Efforts to interview suspects are hampered by language barriers while devices are often encrypted and difficult to analyse, Arumapperuma added.
“The volume of devices we find in each raid is so high, usually about 200 phones and laptops, and we simply do not have the resources to process all of them,” she said.
Adding to the difficulty, experts say, is another factor: Sri Lanka is desperate for foreign exchange. The tourism-dependent country offers visa-free travel to passport holders from 40 countries, including China. It has also opened up investment for online gambling and brick-and-mortar casinos, and has opened up a “special economic zone,” known as Colombo Port City, to attract investors in the digital economy sector.
“Online gambling and offshore gambling operate in legal gray areas in Sri Lanka. The country has an economically distressed project, the Colombo Port City. And then it has a mechanism for bringing large numbers of foreigners,” said Jason Tower, a transnational crime expert at GI-TOC.
In contrast to Southeast Asian scam hubs, where compounds have operated out in public view with protection from politicians and armed groups, Sri Lanka’s scam industry remains clandestine. But failure to tackle these networks could allow the industry to grow to a scale at which criminals become a force powerful enough to defy the government, Tower warned.
"The imagination is the limit. Going from what's hidden and clandestine to what is open and obvious, “ he said.
“Right now Sri Lanka's sort of on the threshold."

Chinese Scam Boss Murdered in Sri Lanka Had Multiple Identities
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-25
03:30:00 UTC
12:30:00 KST

A Chinese cyber scam boss who was kidnapped and murdered in Sri Lanka’s capital in July went by three separate aliases and carried at least two passports, according to documents obtained by OCCRP and The Sunday Times.
Chen Guoqing, 31, was abducted from the Colombo Port City special economic zone in the early hours of July 23 by a group of over a dozen men, one of them brandishing a pistol, according to a copy of the police investigative report into the incident. He was driven to a rural area over 70 kilometers east of Colombo, tortured to death, and his body was abandoned.
The murder of Chen — and the hunt for his killers — received extensive media coverage in Sri Lanka, amid fears that the South Asian country is becoming a new base for Asian criminal syndicates that target victims around the world with sophisticated online fraud schemes.
Sri Lankan police told OCCRP and the Sunday Times that they have arrested five Chinese nationals over the murder and are seeking another three suspects, who are believed to have fled the country. Local authorities have said they believed Chen was involved at a high level in international criminal activity and was murdered over a money dispute with other criminals.
Investigative files show police recovered two passports belonging to the murder victim, each using a different name. One, a Cambodian passport, identified him as Chen Hao. The other, from Suriname, identified him as Tao Guoqing.
Reporters were able to find the murder victim’s real name — Chen Guoqing — by crosschecking his Cambodian passport with a publicly available copy of naturalization and name change records from that country’s Gazette.
Chen’s real name is not mentioned in the Sri Lankan police investigative report, and neither his Cambodian nor his Surinamese aliases have been reported in local media.
Details of Chen’s identity come as OCCRP and the Sunday Times have revealed that, despite over a thousand well-publicized arrests, Sri Lanka has failed to successfully prosecute a single person for using the country as a base to conduct online scams targeting foreigners.
Brian Hanley, the Asia-Pacific Director of the Global Anti-Scam Alliance, said Chen’s murder highlights the vulnerability of Sri Lanka to infiltration by scam syndicates fleeing crackdowns in traditional Southeast Asian epicenters like Cambodia.
“There’s weak enforcement [by Sri Lankan authorities],” Hanley said. “Scams pay. Nobody gets caught. Or if they do, there’s no sanction.”
“For a country like Sri Lanka this level of scam activity could easily start to see a single digit contribution to their entire GDP.”

Updates
Central Election Committee reveals numbers behind preparations for Tuesday's election
The upcoming election will require a nationwide operation involving thousands of polling stations, millions of ballots and about 100,000 workers on election day, according to the Central Elections Committee.
A total of 7,331,981 Israeli citizens are eligible to vote at 12,018 polling stations, with 18,000 ballot boxes in use. Of the polling stations, 6,209 will be accessible, including 3,621 specially accessible stations.
To facilitate travel to the polls, 660 intercity public transportation routes will operate free of charge on election day, including all Israel Railways services.
The Central Elections Committee will print 450 million ballot papers, including 11.5 million for each party list, using a total of 250 tons of paper.
The workforce will expand from 40 employees between election cycles to 1,200 during the election period and approximately 100,000 on election day. Training will cover around 50,000 people in approximately 2,140 classrooms, while some 15,000 cameras will be deployed for election-integrity inspectors.
The budget for the election stands at 690 million shekels (about $223 million), covering the committee's preparations and administration.
Netanyahu shares text warning that failure to reelect him could lead to ‘second holocaust’
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu shared a computer-generated image seeming to depict a nuclear explosion in central Israel, along with a text written by writer Yuval Bloomberg warning that Israel faces an existential threat from Iran and arguing that the country's other political controversies are a distraction from the need to "finish the job" against Tehran.
The text warned voters that choosing a leader unable to "complete the mission" could expose their families to the danger of a "second Holocaust."
"We have another two years of Trump to finish the job in Iran, and there is no way of knowing what will come after that," Bloomberg wrote, warning that Kamala Harris or "some Mamdani equivalent" could succeed the U.S. president.
The Qatargate investigations and the ultra-Orthodox draft were described in the text as "a giant smokescreen" obscuring the Iranian threat.

Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot has asked Israel's attorney general and the Central Elections Committee chairman to cancel a scheduled meeting between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Police Commissioner Danny Levy on election integrity, arguing that the meeting, held without committee representatives, constitutes improper election interference and could undermine public trust in the results.
Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir is set to join the meeting with Netanyahu on Sunday, after Levy refused to attend a similar meeting with Ben-Gvir alone last week.
The national security minister set up a meeting last week on election preparations and summoned Levy and other senior officials. Law enforcement officials criticized the planned meeting, warning that Ben-Gvir, who is running in the election, could use information about police preparations for political purposes.

Yair Golan, leader of Israel's Democrats party, and Ofer Winter, head of the Amcha Israel party, will receive security protection from a private company operating under the direction of Israel's Shin Bet security service, joining former IDF chief Gadi Eisenkot, whose party announced similar arrangements Saturday.
The advisory committee on personal security rejected a request in late August to assign Shin Bet protection to Golan, while recommending that the agency protect Yashar party leader Eisenkot. Last month, the Democrats petitioned the High Court of Justice, seeking to compel the Shin Bet chief, the ministerial committee overseeing the agency and the government to provide security for Golan, citing explicit threats against his life and his family.

He sees Israel becoming an isolated country, its economy increasingly cut off from the rest of the world and forced to make do with Iranian, North Korean or Russian-style schemes to somehow survive.
IDF announces general closure for West Bank Palestinians on Israel's election day
The Israeli military early on Sunday announced that the government had approved its recommendation to ban "the entry and exit of Palestinian workers" throughout the West Bank and to close all land crossings on Israel's Election Day, effectively imposing a general closure on the West Bank on Tuesday.
Additionally, the Israel Defense Forces said that Palestinian workers would not be permitted to enter Israeli settlements in the West Bank for work on Sunday and Monday ahead of the Election, except for "industrial zones and a limited number of other approved areas."
Netanyahu summons police chief after the latter rebuffed Ben-Gvir's election readiness briefing
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu summoned Police Commissioner Danny Levy on Saturday to an unusual meeting on police readiness ahead of Election Day, after the police chief had refused to attend a meeting on the same subject with National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir on Thursday.
Last week, Ben-Gvir convened a meeting and summoned the Commissioner Levy alongside other senior officials. Ultimately, the heads of the Operations Directorate and the Police Operations Division did attend, with Levy authorizing them to provide only a brief overview.

Israel admits forcibly displacing 2,000 Palestinians from Hebron in occupied West Bank

Israel's Defence Minister Israel Katz has acknowledged that Israeli forces forcibly displaced around 2,000 Palestinians from their homes in Hebron in the southern occupied West Bank, barring residents from returning until alleged "Hamas infrastructure" is dismantled.
Katz's remarks to public broadcaster KAN coincided with the second day of an intensive military incursion conducted alongside Shin Bet and Border Police units.
The sweep follows a Friday checkpoint attack in which two Israeli soldiers and two Palestinians were killed, and three other soldiers wounded.
The military subsequently cordoned off Hebron and neighbouring Halhul for an assault projected to last several days.
Official Palestinian news agency Wafa reported that Israeli troops took over evacuated civilian properties in the Khallat Manna and Dahiyat al-Zaytoun districts of southern Hebron to serve as military barracks.
Soldiers also ejected families from homes across other neighbourhoods to establish observation posts, following the forced displacement of hundreds of families amid raids and movement restrictions.
City lockdown
The blockade has paralysed civic life across Hebron. The local education directorate suspended classes on Sunday and Monday, while Hebron University and Al-Quds Open University moved lectures online.
Municipal authorities warned that waste is accumulating inside the city because sealed perimeter entrances prevent rubbish collection teams from reaching external disposal sites.
Near Bethlehem, Israeli forces blocked unpaved bypass routes leading to the town of Tuqu, firing tear gas and stun grenades towards Palestinian vehicles attempting to navigate alternative rough paths amid wider road closures.
The occupied West Bank, including occupied East Jerusalem, has experienced escalating Israeli military incursions and settler violence since the outbreak of Israel's genocidal war on Gaza in October 2023.
Incursions have involved detentions, residential demolitions, the burning of mosques and vehicles, bulldozing of farmland, restriction of agricultural access, and systematic community displacement alongside illegal settlement expansion.

China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-25
11:07:03 CST

TOKYO, Oct. 25 (Xinhua) -- An earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 7.0 on Sunday struck waters near the Ogasawara Islands in the Pacific Ocean, south of Tokyo, with no tsunami warnings issued, the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) said.
The temblor occurred at around 11:10 a.m. local time at a depth of around 470 km in the waters west of the Ogasawara Archipelago, measuring 3 on the Japanese seismic intensity scale of 7 in Chichijima and Hahajima islands, said the weather agency.
The quake's epicenter was located at a latitude of 28.0 degrees north and a longitude of 139.9 degrees east.
There was no threat of a tsunami, the JMA added. ■

LONDON, Oct. 24 (Xinhua) -- British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has called for an open, evidence-based debate on the possibility of restoring free movement between Britain and the EU, as his government considers options for closer ties with the bloc, local media reported Saturday.
"I think you have to have a very factual, quite evidence-based debate about this," Burnham told The Sunday Times in an interview.
The prime minister acknowledged that freedom of movement had posed significant challenges before Brexit, but argued that migration patterns had changed since Britain left the EU.
Burnham said the balance of migration had changed, stressing the need for an "honest discussion" about the differences between past and present migration patterns.
He also highlighted Britain's loss of access to EU migration information-sharing arrangements following Brexit, including Eurodac, the bloc's biometric database used to help manage asylum applications.
But Burnham ruled out recommending that Britain adopt the euro or join the Schengen Area, where internal border checks have largely been abolished.
He is scheduled to meet EU leaders at a summit in Brussels on Nov. 20 and has indicated that he would outline possible options for Britain's future relationship with the bloc at the meeting.
The 2024 election manifesto of the Labour Party, now led by Burnham, ruled out restoring free movement, rejoining the EU single market or entering a customs union.
Burnham has previously pledged to respect those commitments, suggesting that any fundamental change in Britain's relationship with the EU would be unlikely before the next general election. ■

Obama unloads on Trump while stumping for Democrats ahead of midterms
Oct 24 - US President Donald Trump has been telling voters to view the midterm elections as if he were on the ballot, and on Saturday one of his Democratic predecessors did just that.
Ten days out from the elections that will determine control of the closely divided Congress, Barack Obama took to the campaign trail to accuse the Republican president of corruption, deride his strategy for Iran and skewer the gilded aesthetic he has applied to White House renovations.
Obama stumped for Democratic candidates at rallies in Cleveland and Detroit, lampooning the Trump administration. Campaigning in Michigan for US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, Obama framed the November 3 vote as a "circuit breaker" to "at least rein in some of the foolishness" of Trump's presidency.
"We got to flip that circuit breaker, bring some accountability to this government," Obama said.
Obama, president from 2009 until Trump began his first term in 2017, remains one of the most popular figures among Democrats. They hope that bringing him into the race can fire up their supporters for a tight US Senate race in which El-Sayed faces Republican Mike Rogers, a former US representative.
The former president obliged the Michigan crowd by playing to Democrats' frequently repeated criticisms of Trump and of Republicans' willingness to go along with him.
"We have never seen a president excel in straight-up grifting, on your dime, like this," Obama said. "Never seen a president so intent on selling favors like this ... Now the party seems to stand for corrupt government, or inept government, or no government."
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll in August found that 63% of Americans think the president and his family have inappropriately profited from cryptocurrency since he returned to the White House last year and that 69% believe his policy decisions are influenced by his private business dealings.
Obama also ridiculed the administration's claims of victory against Iran. He argued that the war has given Iran more economic leverage because its threats to attack shipping in the Strait of Hormuz have unsettled oil exporters.
"Iran now has veto power over the Strait of Hormuz, where oil goes through to get to the world," Obama said.

Armed assailants on motorcycles have killed at least 20 people in a raid on the rural village of Binnari in Nigeria's Taraba state, survivors confirmed, marking the latest deadly assault across the country's vulnerable rural communities.
The gunmen opened fire immediately following Friday prayers, triggering panic as residents fled into surrounding bushland.
"People were running in different directions to escape the attack. Nobody knew where it was safe to go," resident Isiyaku Musa said.

Taraba state, situated towards central Nigeria, has faced mounting violence from criminal "bandit" networks.
Amnesty International Nigeria condemned the state's security response, arguing that authorities continue to abandon northern rural communities to armed gangs acting with impunity.
"Consistent failure of the authorities to bring the suspected perpetrators to justice is clearly emboldening impunity," the rights organisation stated on social media.

Lan reclaims rings world title as five teams share apparatus golds
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-25
10:18:33 CST
11:18:33 KST

ROTTERDAM, Netherlands, Oct. 24 (Xinhua) -- China's Lan Xingyu reclaimed the men's rings world title after a five-year wait on Saturday, with five nations sharing the gold medals on the opening day of apparatus finals at the World Artistic Gymnastics Championships.
Lan scored 14.766 points to finish 0.433 ahead of Greece's Eleftherios Petrounias, who took silver with 14.333. Armenia's Artur Avetisyan claimed bronze with 14.233.
Competing sixth in the eight-man final, Lan combined the highest difficulty score in the field, 6.000, with an execution mark of 8.766 to secure China's first men's gold of the championships.
The 28-year-old previously won the rings title in Kitakyushu, Japan, in 2021 and took bronze at last year's championships in Jakarta.
American Frederick Richard won the men's floor exercise title with 14.633, edging Britain's defending champion Jake Jarman by just 0.033. Israel's Artem Dolgopyat finished third with 14.466.
Armenia celebrated another title through Hamlet Manukyan, who scored 15.300 on pommel horse. Italy's Gabriele Targhetta earned silver with 15.233, while Armenia's Mamikon Khachatryan completed the podium with 15.000. Japan's Daiki Hashimoto finished eighth with 13.466.
Brazil's Rebeca Andrade took the women's vault crown with 14.466, ahead of Americans Claire Pease and Skye Blakely, who scored 14.233 and 14.166 respectively.
Algeria's Kaylia Nemour won the uneven bars with 15.333, combining a difficulty score of 7.000 with 8.333 for execution. Germany's Helen Kevric secured silver with 14.833, while Blakely collected another bronze with 14.600.
Lan's victory came after China won bronze in Tuesday's men's team final, where the squad scored 249.193 behind Japan's 251.928 and Russia's 250.329. All three teams secured qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
China competed without injured all-around standout Zhang Boheng. Despite recording the highest team totals on rings and parallel bars, mistakes elsewhere left the squad third overall.
The championships conclude on Sunday with finals in men's vault, parallel bars and horizontal bar, and women's balance beam and floor exercise. China's Zou Jingyuan will seek a record-extending fifth world parallel bars title. ■

Cuba extends daylight saving time to counter impact from U.S. blockade
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-25
10:18:01 CST
11:18:01 KST

HAVANA, Oct. 24 (Xinhua) -- Cuba will maintain daylight saving time until Nov. 7, 2027 to mitigate its power generation shortfall, which has been exacerbated by tighter U.S. sanctions and fuel supply restrictions, local authorities said Saturday.
The measure is expected to reduce evening peak demand by about 126 megawatts (MW), helping curb power outages, according to a joint statement by the Ministry of Energy and Mines and the Ministry of Labor and Social Security.
Of the estimated savings, 76 MW will come from reduced electricity consumption for artificial lighting and 50 MW from solar photovoltaic generation, the statement said.
To minimize disruptions to morning activities, schools and workplaces will open 30 minutes later from Nov. 1, 2026 to March 14, 2027, when standard time would normally be in effect.
Cuba has faced a severe blackout crisis for nearly two years, which worsened in January 2026 after the U.S. government threatened to impose sanctions on countries supplying fuel to the island. Havana has condemned the measure as violation of international law. ■

Midwest muso Kevin Morby is no longer America's best kept secret
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-25
02:00:00 UTC
11:00:00 KST

Kevin Morby on famous friends, mortality and touring Little Wide Open in Australia
During the 2020 pandemic, US singer-songwriter Kevin Morby almost got stuck in Australia.
As quarantines tightened, he found himself in Melbourne before it had some of the world's toughest lockdowns.
He didn't panic. Instead, he remembers thinking:
"If I have to start a new life, this is a pretty good place to do so."
He has become acquainted with Australia's bigger cities over multiple visits.
"Feel[ing] like, 'Oh, I know where I'm at. I know this neighbourhood — I love that one restaurant! It's nice," he tells Double J's Henry Wagons.
That moment of acceptance speaks to something essential about Morby, a folk-rock journeyman who finds belonging and meaning in transit.
That philosophy feels more relevant than ever as Morby returns to tour Australia next month, supporting his latest album Little Wide Open.
Following a discography inspired by adopted homes — Laurel Canyon (2016's Singing Saw), New York (2017's City Music), Memphis (2022's This Is A Photograph) — Morby's eighth solo album heads back to the Missouri farmlands and Kansas City suburbs where he grew up.
"I have a complicated relationship to it, just as most people do with their home towns. There's a lot of love and a lot of resentment. It's all these emotions and a lot of them come out on this record."
The Midwest and musical influences
A collection of sentimental alt-country, dusky folk and lush Americana, Little Wide Open conjures rich imagery: fields of sunflowers and June bugs, late-night bars and long highways stretching into flat horizons dominated by wide open skies.
Porchside strumming and finger-picking score vivid portraits of "anywhere America" on songs with names like Cowtown and Bible Belt.
Small-town iconography and spangling riffs power 100,000, before a guitar explodes like a Fourth of July firecracker over the song's climax.
These tunes, built from tried-and-true chords and Morby's humble Dylanesque voice, romanticise the comforts of small towns but equally yearn to escape them for something larger.
For Morby, the Midwest is simple.
"I don't mean that in a derogatory sense. The lifestyles are simpler. There's a quality of life, your money goes further, things like that. But with that, there's less opportunity and less culture.
"There can be great things about the Midwest.
"I feel if you use the time and space and the boredom to your advantage, those don't have to necessarily be bad things."
You can hear the influence of Morby's "big five": Bob Dylan, Leonard Cohen, Lou Reed, Nina Simone, and Townes Van Zandt.
But also, more pluck and twang ("Country music's great. One of [music's] backbones over the past two centuries") as well as the "rootsy, heartland rock and roll" Morby was immersed in making the record.
"I bought this pick-up truck with a free subscription to satellite radio. Part of that was the Tom Petty radio station and I just got super into him. He was a big influence."
He also cites the album World Without Tears by legendary artist Lucinda Williams, who provides a drawling, cautionary spoken word on stand-out track Natural Disaster.
"I wanted this voice-of-God thing to come in. I was so thrilled when she said she'd do it."
Williams isn't Little Wide Open's only notable guest.
Famous friends
In a sign of how esteemed Morby is among his peers, the album also features Bon Iver's Justin Vernon (emulating a tornado siren on rustic opener Badlands), backing vocals from MUNA's Katie Gavin, and players from Florence + The Machine, Perfume Genius, Sylvan Esso and Hand Habits.
Then there's The National's Aaron Dessner. Fresh from producing blockbuster records for Taylor Swift and Ed Sheeran, Dessner recorded Little Wide Open at his studio in upstate New York.
"He made the songs feel big and dense in their ways without distracting the story or the vocal," Morby explains.
"He really kept my vocal front and centre. It felt like I was standing a little bit naked on these recordings, but I think it benefited the album in the end.
"Besides that, he's just an unbelievable musician. And really believed in these songs through moments where maybe I wasn't believing in them … 'Kevin, you gotta let these songs breathe.'"
Dessner's fingerprints are all over Junebug, with its gossamer guitars and piano decorated by oboe and harp. But those flourishes never overshadow Morby.
"Sometimes the myth grows bigger than the dream" he sings on the swooning title track, where banjo, slide guitar and fiddle comfortably sprawl past the eight-minute mark.
Getting older (and better)
Little Wide Open is also charged by Morby "looking down the barrel of 40," and the sense of life moving too fast.
"Am I a has-been? Am I a husband?" he sings ruefully amid the otherwise upbeat Javelin. Nearly cut for being too vulnerable, the lyric was prompted by impending parenthood.
Morby recently welcomed his first child alongside his musician-partner Katie Crutchfield, better known as alt-country favourite Waxahatchee.
"We fell in love on tour. We're these creative sounding boards for one other. I really trust Katie's ear and her thoughts. It's real easy to walk in the other room and say, 'Hey, is this lyric good?'"
While she doesn't feature on Little Wide Open, "Katie is very much in the DNA. It's a lot of love songs," Morby says.
"It's a funny thing being in a public relationship because people are going to know who you're singing about."
Because Morby's music is presented with such easy-going charm, you can easily miss the serious subject matter of his lyrics, which contemplate existential questions about life, time and mortality.
"It's a darker song [but] for the longest time, I wanted to call the record I Ride Passenger," Morby says of a tune loosely inspired by a fan who died in a car crash on his way to see him perform.
The central lyric? "If time is a violent driver, then we ride passenger."
Die Young is a warm, mid-tempo reflection on aging, and surviving the fragile existence of a touring musician.
That idea is revisited on the plaintive closer, Field Guide for The Butterflies, which uses insects splattered on windshields as a metaphor for troubadours compelled to reach and share deeper truths despite the risks of lonely lives spent on the road.
But "it's not suicide if I die out chasing thrills" Morby confides in the album's closing moments. "Just me trying to grow wings."
It's a moving finish to a record where Morby ponders where he's been, what happens next and what it all means.
Kevin Morby's tour begins in Eltham on Thursday, November 12, before shows in Bellingen, Brisbane, Mt Glorious, Sydney, Brunswick Heads, Castlemaine and Melbourne.

Hong Kong needs a civil service fit for a changed world
Beyond administrative expertise, civil servants must now master technology, cross-departmental cooperation and strategic flexibility
Hong Kong’s civil service has long enjoyed a reputation for efficiency, professionalism and probity. It has also been a pillar of stability, particularly during the transition from British to Chinese rule.
Outside the general and administrative grades, many civil servants spend much of their careers in relatively specialised areas of responsibility. This allows them to develop deep expertise and makes them dependable regulators and administrators. However, it can also make it harder to adapt when new challenges cut across established departmental boundaries.
Hong Kong was once a British outpost built on trade. Government played a relatively limited role in economic development, while free trade, market forces and the city’s strategic position at the crossroads of East and West helped it prosper.

Sri Lanka launched its national anti-narcotics drive "A Nation United" on Oct. 30 last year. Official data indicated that more than 303,000 suspects were arrested as of Oct. 18. ■

IN BRIEF: Brazil to hold second round of presidential elections

Unknown Publisher
2026-10-25
01:15:01 UTC
10:15:01 KST

RIO DE JANEIRO, October 25. /TASS/. The second, decisive round of the general election will take place in Brazil. Voters will decide who will serve as head of state for the next four years: incumbent President and Workers’ Party leader Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva or the candidate from the right-wing opposition, senator Flavio Bolsonaro.
Voting procedure
Voting in Brazil will take place from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. local time (11:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. GMT). More than 158.7 million Brazilian citizens are eligible to vote. Voting is mandatory for all literate Brazilians between the ages of 18 and 69.
Key candidates
Incumbent President Lula da Silva is seeking re-election for what would be the final term of his political career. He is building his campaign around strengthening Brazil’s international standing and expanding export opportunities, particularly with countries in the Global South and the BRICS. His domestic policy agenda includes tax reform, government funding for defense and technology initiatives, and actively developing hydrocarbon reserves.
Meanwhile, Flavio Bolsonaro is focusing his campaign on strongly condemning the government’s policies and drawing public attention to the excessive tax burden and rampant street crime. The right-wing opposition candidate has rallied the conservative electorate and powerful agricultural interests behind him. In foreign policy, he favors the US market and aims to restore bilateral relations to the level seen during the administrations of Jair Bolsonaro and Donald Trump.
First-round results, political landscape
The October 4 vote showed an advantage for conservative forces and fell short of the incumbent president’s expectations, falling short of the incumbent president’s expectations of a first-round victory. According to the results, Flavio Bolsonaro took the lead with 47.03% of the vote. Lula da Silva is in second place with 45.16%. The margin between the candidates was less than two percentage points. Given an electorate of 150 million, this is equal to nearly two to three million votes.
On the eve of the second round, the son of the former Brazilian leader is considered the frontrunner. Flavio Bolsonaro managed to seize the political initiative by successfully mobilizing voters in economically developed regions and the agricultural business sector.
Lula da Silva’s campaign shifted to a defensive strategy between the rounds, finding itself playing catch-up. The government passed emergency social measures, including debt relief for four million self-employed individuals and an unexpected increase in benefits for the poor.
